title: Sparsely Shared LoRA on Whisper for Child Speech Recognition
status: arXiv:2309.11756, submitted 2023; publication venue not verified in this pass
read_scope: Read abstract; method sections on LoRA, AdaLoRA, and S2-LoRA; dataset and adaptation settings; result tables 1-2 and conclusion. PDF is 5 pages. No code or experiment rerun.
key_evidence: CSRC-2021 child speech includes 28.6 h read and 29.5 h conversational Mandarin; the adaptation study uses the 28.6 h read set, with 1K/10K/30K utterance subsets. S2-LoRA shares low-rank matrices and learns sparse rank coefficients; it is competitive in-domain and improves out-of-domain generalization with 0.02% trainable parameters. PEFT can outperform full FT in this setup; full FT often degraded on larger Whisper models at 1K examples. Cantonese performance worsened under Mandarin adaptation, discussed as language-ID/token modeling conflict.
